item.description:
What's new in 2.32.0

Two new tools. Herdr runs a herd of coding agents in one window — connect a folder, add agents, split them across the screen and watch them all work. Clip to Link records a corner of your screen and hands back a link to the clip. There's also a home screen now, so the app has somewhere to land, and a shelf of badges on it that fills up as you use Dax.

Herdr ⌃⌥.

  • Mission control for coding agents. Connect a folder and Herdr opens a window of live terminals — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, whichever you use — running side by side in the same project. Add an agent from a menu of them; you never open a raw shell you then have to type into.
  • Split by dragging. Drag a pane against the edge of another and the space divides between them. Even Out Terminals squares up the seams without restarting anything, because a real re-layout would kill every process in the window.
  • A tree that tells you what's running. Groups hold agents, agents show their brand and say when they're working. Rename anything, close anything, collapse the sidebar out of the way.
  • Green fills the screen rather than taking it over — the menu bar and the Dock stay where they are, so a wall of terminals doesn't cost you the rest of your Mac.

Clip to Link ⌃⌥;

  • Record a region, get a link. Drag a box round the part of the screen worth showing, record, and the clip uploads and the link lands on your clipboard. GIF, MP4 or MOV — the format you used last is the one it offers next.
  • GIFs that move at the speed they were recorded. Frames are read in order with the timestamps they were captured at, so a pause is a pause and a fast bit is fast, instead of the whole clip playing at several times life.
  • Clips have sound, MOV shows what it weighs before you send it, and 15 and 30 fps are back — they divide the capture rate evenly, so no frames are dropped unevenly to reach them.

A home screen

  • Somewhere to land. Dax is a menu-bar app with no windows of its own, so finishing setup used to leave nothing on screen and everything behind a shortcut you hadn't learnt yet. The Dock icon now opens a page with your face, your name, and the three keys worth knowing.
  • A shelf of badges under your photo, filling up as you use Dax. Click one for its page, or the tail of the stack for the whole case — every badge there is, earned and not, with what each one takes.
  • Your photo is a control. Hover it to change it, or open it full size.

Notifications

  • Do Not Disturb ⌃⌥Z — silence every toast without leaving what you're doing.
  • Toasts go to Notification Centre too, and the ones that ask you something can be answered from there.
  • Hovering a toast holds it still. Reading a long one was a race against its own countdown, and both ways to act on it are targets you have to be on the card to hit.

Also in this release

  • Logging out takes the session with it. Every window that was about a signed-in person closes, none of them open again until you sign in, and the page says "Signing out…" while it happens rather than vanishing mid-click.
  • A server having a bad minute now says so in a sentence — and retries once, quietly, which is usually all it takes — instead of handing you a gateway's stack trace.
  • Snips photograph the screen before the menu can close, so you can capture a menu or a popover that would otherwise disappear as you reach for it.
  • Annotate opens behind a scrim that tells you ⌘↩ sends, and has a blur tool for anything you'd rather not include.
  • Settings closes on Escape, palettes have a Back button for when ⎋ isn't obvious, and there's a Licenses pane with the terms in full.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
